A comprehensive go-to-market strategy for this US-based digital therapeutics company launching its prescription smoking-cessation app in both the UK and Germany within the next 18 months should address three key areas: clinical evidence, regulatory compliance, and reimbursement economics. Here's a defensible plan for each:

1. Clinical Evidence:
a) Conduct a post-marketing surveillance study in the US to gather real-world data on safety and efficacy.
b) Translate the existing US clinical trial data into German and English to support local regulatory submissions.
c) Engage with UK and German medical experts to design and conduct local studies, if necessary, to address any regional concerns or requirements.

2. Regulatory Compliance:
a) Obtain CE marking for the app in accordance with EU Medical Device Directive (MDD) 93/42/EEC and EU In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Directive (IVDD) 98/79/EC.
b) Submit a UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) Class IIa medical device application, as appropriate for the app's intended use.
c) Engage with local regulatory authorities to address any specific requirements or concerns.

3. Data-Protection Law:
a) Ensure compliance with EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK-GDPR).
b) Develop a data privacy policy that addresses local regulations, patient rights, and transparency.
c) Implement appropriate technical measures to protect sensitive personal data.

4. Reimbursement Economics:
a) Engage with local health authorities in both countries to explore potential reimbursement pathways for the app.
b) Conduct an economic evaluation of the app's cost-effectiveness compared to existing smoking-cessation treatments.
c) Develop a pricing strategy that takes into account local healthcare systems, patient needs, and market dynamics.

5. Marketing Strategy:
a) Establish partnerships with local healthcare providers, payers, and advocacy groups to promote awareness and adoption.
b) Develop targeted marketing campaigns in both countries, leveraging digital channels and local media outlets.
c) Provide educational resources for healthcare professionals and patients on the app's use and benefits.

6. Sales and Distribution:
a) Identify local distributors or partners with experience in medical device sales and distribution.
b) Establish a robust supply chain to ensure timely delivery of the app to customers.
c) Develop training programs for local sales teams, customer support staff, and healthcare professionals.

7. Post-Market Surveillance:
a) Implement a continuous monitoring program to track safety and efficacy data from both countries.
b) Engage with local medical experts to address any emerging issues or concerns.
c) Use the collected data to inform future product development and regulatory submissions.

By addressing these key areas, this US-based digital therapeutics company can develop a defensible go-to-market plan for launching its prescription smoking-cessation app in both the UK and Germany within the next 18 months.
